{{nihongo|'''Hine Shrine'''|日根神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumi Province]].

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} in Hine District of {{ill|Izumi Province|Q1047117|qid=Q1047117}}, and the fifth-ranked shrine (gonomiya) of Izumi Province. Its otabisho stands along the {{ill|Kumano Kaidō|Q11568976|qid=Q11568976}} (Kishu Kaido / Wakayama-Kaizuka Line) in {{ill|Nagataki|Q11653347|qid=Q11653347|lt=Nagataki}} in the same city.

=== History ===
The founding time is unclear. Shrine tradition says that during {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ar|الإمبراطور جينمو|arz|الامبراطور جينمو|as|জিম্মু|az|Cimmu|bcl|Emperador Jimmu|be|Імператар Дзіму|ca|Jinmu|cdo|Sìng-ū Tiĕng-huòng|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر جینمو|cs|Džimmu|de|Jimmu|el|Αυτοκράτορας Τζίμου|eo|Imperiestro Jinmu|es|Jinmu Tennō|et|Jimmu|eu|Jimmu enperadorea|fa|امپراتور جینمو|fi|Jinmu|fr|Jinmu|hak|Sṳ̀n-vú Thiên-fòng|he|ג'ימו, קיסר יפן|hi|सम्राट जिममु|hr|Jinmu|hu|Dzsinmu japán császár|id|Jimmu|it|Jinmu|ja|神武天皇|jv|Jimmu Tenno|ka|ძიმუ|ko|진무 천황|kw|Emperour Jimmu|la|Jimmu|lt|Imperatorius Džinmu|lv|Džimmu|mn|Эзэн Хаан Жиммү|mr|जिम्मू|ms|Maharaja Jimmu|my|ဂျင်းမူ ဧကရာဇ်|nl|Jimmu|no|Jimmu|pl|Jimmu|pt|Jimmu|ru|Император Дзимму|sh|Car Jimmu|simple|Emperor Jimmu|sl|Cesar Džinmu|sr|Џинму|sv|Jimmu|th|จักรพรรดิจิมมุ|tl|Emperador Jimmu|tr|Jimmu|uk|Імператор Дзімму|uz|Jimmu|vi|Thiên hoàng Jimmu|war|Emperador Jimmu|wuu|神武天皇|zh|神武天皇|zh_classical|神武天皇|zh_min_nan|Sîn-bú Thian-hông|zh_yue|神武天皇|qid=Q200188|lt=Kamuyamato Iwarebiko-no-Mikoto}}'s eastern campaign, he fought {{ill|Nagatsuhiko|Q4922278|qid=Q4922278}} when entering {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato}} from {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi}} and was defeated. Retreating to this field area, he enshrined the deity of "Hi" (heaven/day), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu Omikami}}, and the deity of "Ne" (the underworld), {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}}. After winning and pacifying Yamato, the area was named "Hineno" and the shrine became Hine Shrine.

It is counted among the {{ill|Izumi Inoue Shrine|Q11554710|qid=Q11554710}} established in {{ill|716|Q23531|qid=Q23531}} ({{ill|Reiki (era)|Q1373115|qid=Q1373115}} 2), and is listed among the ten Engishiki shrines of Hine District, indicating a history of over 1200 years. In {{ill|673|Q31105|qid=Q31105}} (Emperor {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|qid=Q335181}} 2), the shrine-temple Muhenko-in (present {{ill|Jigen-in Temple|Q11495035|qid=Q11495035}}) was built adjacent to the precinct.

In the reign of {{ill|Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|qid=Q349263}}, during the great drought of {{ill|742|Q23601|qid=Q23601}} ({{ill|Tenpyō|Q1199879|qid=Q1199879}} 14), the shrine received 500 koku from the court.

[[Image:HineJinjaHonden.jpg|right|200px|thumb|Hine Shrine main hall ({{ill|Azuchi–Momoyama period|Q319531|qid=Q319531|lt=Momoyama period}}, {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}})]]

It was burned in warfare during the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} era (1573-1593), and its lands were confiscated by {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550|lt=Hashiba Hideyoshi}} in 1585. In {{ill|1602|Q6727|qid=Q6727}} ({{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 7), shrine buildings were rebuilt by {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyori|be|Таётомі Хідэёры|ca|Toyotomi Hideyori|cs|Hidejori Tojotomi|de|Toyotomi Hideyori|el|Τογιοτόμι Χιντεγιόρι|eo|Toyotomi Hideyori|es|Toyotomi Hideyori|eu|Toyotomi Hideyori|fa|تویوتومی هیده‌یوری|fi|Toyotomi Hideyori|fr|Toyotomi Hideyori|id|Toyotomi Hideyori|it|Toyotomi Hideyori|ja|豊臣秀頼|ko|도요토미 히데요리|la|Fideyorus|lt|Tojotomi Hidejori|ms|Toyotomi Hideyori|nl|Toyotomi Hideyori|no|Toyotomi Hideyori|pl|Hideyori Toyotomi|pt|Toyotomi Hideyori|ru|Тоётоми Хидэёри|sk|Hidejori Tojotomi|sr|Тојотоми Хидејори|th|โทโยโตมิ ฮิเดโยริ|tr|Toyotomi Hideyori|uk|Тойотомі Хідейорі|vi|Toyotomi Hideyori|zh|豐臣秀賴|qid=Q313641}}.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} era, it was separated from adjacent Muhenko-in by {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ca|Shinbutsu bunri|de|Shinbutsu-Bunri|es|Shinbutsu bunri|fa|شینبوتسو بونری|fi|Shinbutsu bunri|fr|Shinbutsu bunri|id|Shinbutsu bunri|it|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離|ru|Симбуцу бунри|tr|Şinbutsu-bunri|zh|神佛分離|qid=Q1970535}}. In {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} (Meiji 6), it was designated as gosha; in {{ill|1924|Q2173|qid=Q2173}} ({{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 13), promoted to fūsha. The main hall was designated Osaka Prefecture tangible cultural property (Building No. 20) on March 31, {{ill|1972|Q2476|qid=Q2476}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 47). {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Oizeki Natural Park}} is adjacent.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* Principal deities - {{ill|Ugayafukiaezu|Q1373935|qid=Q1373935|lt=Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Q3082751|qid=Q3082751|lt=Tamayorihime-no-Mikoto}}, four princes (Itsuse-no-Mikoto, Inahi-no-Mikoto, Mikenuma-no-Mikoto, {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ar|الإمبراطور جينمو|arz|الامبراطور جينمو|as|জিম্মু|az|Cimmu|bcl|Emperador Jimmu|be|Імператар Дзіму|ca|Jinmu|cdo|Sìng-ū Tiĕng-huòng|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر جینمو|cs|Džimmu|de|Jimmu|el|Αυτοκράτορας Τζίμου|eo|Imperiestro Jinmu|es|Jinmu Tennō|et|Jimmu|eu|Jimmu enperadorea|fa|امپراتور جینمو|fi|Jinmu|fr|Jinmu|hak|Sṳ̀n-vú Thiên-fòng|he|ג'ימו, קיסר יפן|hi|सम्राट जिममु|hr|Jinmu|hu|Dzsinmu japán császár|id|Jimmu|it|Jinmu|ja|神武天皇|jv|Jimmu Tenno|ka|ძიმუ|ko|진무 천황|kw|Emperour Jimmu|la|Jimmu|lt|Imperatorius Džinmu|lv|Džimmu|mn|Эзэн Хаан Жиммү|mr|जिम्मू|ms|Maharaja Jimmu|my|ဂျင်းမူ ဧကရာဇ်|nl|Jimmu|no|Jimmu|pl|Jimmu|pt|Jimmu|ru|Император Дзимму|sh|Car Jimmu|simple|Emperor Jimmu|sl|Cesar Džinmu|sr|Џинму|sv|Jimmu|th|จักรพรรดิจิมมุ|tl|Emperador Jimmu|tr|Jimmu|uk|Імператор Дзімму|uz|Jimmu|vi|Thiên hoàng Jimmu|war|Emperador Jimmu|wuu|神武天皇|zh|神武天皇|zh_classical|神武天皇|zh_min_nan|Sîn-bú Thian-hông|zh_yue|神武天皇|qid=Q200188|lt=Wakamikenu-no-Mikoto}}), Okishitomi-no-sukune

=== Precincts ===
[[Image:HimeJinja.jpg|right|200px|thumb|Hime Shrine]]
* Main hall (Osaka Prefecture designated tangible cultural property) - rebuilt in {{ill|1602|Q6727|qid=Q6727}} (Keicho 7) by Toyotomi Hideyori.
* Haiden - rebuilt in Keicho 7 (1602) by Toyotomi Hideyori.
* Shinmon gate
* Shrine office - formerly Shimonobo, a sub-temple of Muhenko-in (present {{ill|Jigen-in Temple|Q11495035|qid=Q11495035}}).
* Hime Shrine (Osaka Prefecture designated tangible cultural property) - deities: {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Ohirume no Muchi no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}}. A Shikinaisha. Listed as official shrine in {{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}} ({{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} 1) under Emperor {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|Q349243|qid=Q349243}}.
* Niu Shrine (Nonomiya) - deities: Niutsuhime Omikami (Wakahirume-no-Mikoto), Niu Koya Miko Omikami ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kariba Myojin}}). Said to have been invited in Tenpyo 30 of Emperor Shomu. Original shrine is {{ill|Niutsuhime Shrine|Q705154|qid=Q705154|lt=Niu Tsuhime Shrine}} (Amano Taisha) in Kamiamano, Katsuragi, Ito District, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|Q131314|qid=Q131314}}. Festival held October 10.
* {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|Q1129330|qid=Q1129330|lt=Ebisu}}-miya (sub-shrine of Niu Shrine) - deity: {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|fa|کوتوشیرونوشی|fr|Kotoshironushi|it|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主|ko|고토시로누시|ru|Котосиронуси|simple|Kotoshironushi|th|โคโตชิโรนูชิ|zh|事代主神|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi}} no Mikoto. Origins unclear; records mention rename after transfer in Tenpo 11 and merger of three deities into Niu Shrine at current location in Meiji 41.
* Okamae Shrine
* Otabisho
